subject: Agriculture
title: Parasites and Deworming
description: Learn Parasites and Deworming in one minute.

hook.text: Internal parasites cost the global livestock industry over $3 billion annually in lost productivity.

buildup.text: Gastrointestinal worms infect grazing animals worldwide, causing weight loss, anemia, and death in severe cases.

discovery.text: Anthelmintic drugs revolutionized livestock health in the 1960s, enabling intensive grazing systems.

twist.text: Worms are evolving resistance to every drug class. Some farms have parasites that nothing can kill.

climax.text: Targeted selective treatment—deworming only sick animals—slows resistance by maintaining a susceptible worm population.

punchline.text: Treating every animal bred invincible worms. Treating fewer saves the drugs.

quiz.question: Why is targeted selective deworming preferred over treating all animals?
options: It slows parasite resistance by maintaining susceptible worm populations

details.summary: Internal and external parasites cost the global livestock industry billions annually through reduced growth, lower milk yield, and animal death. This topic covers major livestock parasites, deworming strategies, and the growing problem of anthelmintic resistance.
details.whyItMatters: Parasitic infections are the most common health problem in grazing livestock. Anthelmintic resistance is spreading rapidly, threatening the primary method of parasite control worldwide.
takeaways: Gastrointestinal worms are the most economically important parasites of grazing livestock
Routine deworming with anthelmintics has driven widespread drug resistance in parasites
Targeted selective treatment—deworming only heavily infected animals—slows resistance

faq.question: Why are parasites such a big problem for livestock?
faq.answer: Gastrointestinal worms, liver flukes, ticks, and other parasites drain nutrients, cause anemia, reduce growth and milk production, and can kill young or heavily infected animals. In grazing systems, reinfection from contaminated pastures is constant.

faq.question: What is anthelmintic resistance and why is it dangerous?
faq.answer: Parasites evolve resistance to deworming drugs when the same chemicals are used repeatedly without rotation. Resistance to all three major drug classes has been documented worldwide, and no new anthelmintic classes have been developed in decades.
